newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Helwan cement 96/7 H1 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Helwan cement 96/7 H1 profit up.

text.p: Helwan Portland Cement profit rose in the first six months of financial year 1996/97 to 75.4 million pounds ($22.2 million) from 54.8 million pounds in the same period the previous year, a statement said on Monday.
The financial year started on July 1.

The statement published in al-Akhbar newspaper said that production rose 23 percent to 307.3 million and revenues were 344.8 million pounds in the first six months of 1996/97 against 269.6 million in the same last-year period.

In December, the state sold an additional 22.3 percent stake in Helwan, reducing the state holding company's stake to 47.9 percent and in January Helwan appointed a new board of directors and officially changed its legal status from a state-owned firm to the private sector.
Corporate sources said the firm was expecting profits of 180 million pounds ($53 million) for the current financial year. Net profits in the first quarter of 1996/97 were 35 million pounds.

Under its new private status, the firm's financial year will change to the calendar year instead of beginning on July 1. The sources said the 1996/7 financial year would run an extra six months to end on December 31 instead of June 30.
